mainEntity.name: Do you provide specialty clinic cleaning in Reading, MA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Reading (Middlesex County) is one of the 109 Massachusetts cities and towns we serve. It is about 26 miles northeast of our Marlborough base in a straight line. Every engagement starts with a free on-site assessment; call (978) 307-8107.

mainEntity.name: Which Reading ZIP codes do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: All of them: 01867. If your facility sits on a town line, tell us the street address and we will confirm.

mainEntity.name: Are there specialty clinics in Reading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reading's verified healthcare anchor is Winchester Hospital Reading Health Center (outpatient center), and practices operate in and around it. We have not verified an individual specialty clinic by name yet; tell us your address and we will confirm scheduling.

mainEntity.name: We have four specialties sharing one suite. Can one protocol cover all of them?

acceptedAnswer.text: One contract, yes. One protocol, no. Dermatology procedure rooms, ophthalmology lanes with coated optics, ENT reprocessing areas, and allergy testing rooms carry different soil loads, different device instructions, and different acceptable chemistries. We map the suite by room type and equipment, assign products and frequency per zone, and use color-coded microfiber so nothing transfers between them. Section II items A and B of the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist expect frequently touched surfaces to be cleaned and then disinfected, with products used to the manufacturer's dilution, storage, shelf life, and contact time.

mainEntity.name: What do you do with a device that has no cleaning instructions at all?

acceptedAnswer.text: We do not invent a method for it. Where a manufacturer provides no cleaning and disinfection instructions, CDC's position is that the item is not suitable for multi-patient use, and improvising a chemistry risks either damaging the device or leaving it contaminated with no way to prove otherwise. We list every such device in the walkthrough report and hand it back to your administrator to resolve with the vendor. That is usually a short email and a returned document, and it closes a finding before a surveyor opens one.

mainEntity.name: What would you produce if Massachusetts DPH or AAAHC arrived tomorrow?

acceptedAnswer.text: The responsibility matrix showing which surfaces and devices are ours and which are clinical, the written cleaning and decontamination schedule under 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(i), product labels with EPA registration numbers and contact times, SDS sheets, the chemical storage and utility closet arrangement against 105 CMR 140.206, crew training records, and dated service logs. Surveyors test whether the method was defined and followed, not whether the floor looks clean. Dory's also carries $2 million in general liability and will issue a certificate naming your clinic.

Citations Reading specialty clinics can avoid

Real, published regulatory findings — every citation links to its source.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, semi-critical item definition and High-Level Disinfection items A to C

Semi-critical instruments and probes — those contacting mucous membranes or non-intact skin — given only a surface wipe rather than at least high-level disinfection, and not pre-cleaned first.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist, non-critical item definition; CDC Core Practices 5f

Shared non-critical devices used across a procedure day — blood pressure cuffs, chin rests, headrests, positioning equipment — not cleaned and disinfected between patients according to the degree of contamination.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section II items A and B

Frequently touched surfaces in the procedure room not cleaned and then disinfected, and products not used to the manufacturer's dilution, storage, shelf-life and contact time.

How we clean specialty clinics in Reading

Where contamination concentrates

  • Procedure chairs and tables
  • Equipment control panels and handles
  • Waiting-room seating
  • Restroom fixtures
  • Sink and dispenser surfaces
  • Exam-room chairs

What the crew does, in order

  1. Clean environmental surfaces around the equipment with products compatible with its finishes.
  2. Leave instruments, probes and patient-care devices to clinical staff.
  3. Empty trash; sharps and regulated waste stay with your licensed hauler.
  4. Damp-mop floors, including under procedure chairs.
  5. Log rooms completed and anything the clinic needs to address.

How often

  • Procedure rooms: environmental surfaces daily, patient-contact surfaces between patients by clinical staff.
  • Exam and consult rooms: daily.
  • Periodic: walls, vents and high dusting.

Specialty clinics usually need after-hours cleaning so procedure rooms are ready for the first case.

Records for your surveyors

  • Safety Data Sheets
  • Signed service logs
  • Bloodborne pathogen training records
  • Certificate of insurance

Questions worth asking at the walkthrough

  • How do you sequence a procedure room versus a consult room?
  • What documentation will you leave after each visit?
  • How do you train staff on a new clinic's equipment?

We answer each of these in writing after the free assessment.
